evals.prompt: Voici la fiche de ma naine guerrière, quelque chose cloche mais je ne trouve pas quoi. Tu peux vérifier ?
evals.expected_output: A French audit reporting the four real defects — the +2 Con/+1 Wis species bonus (a 2014 rule; in 2024 the ability increase comes from the background), the stated HP of 15 against a computed 14, Arcana, which is not on the fighter skill list, and darkvision stated at 18 m where the catalog grants the Dwarf 36 m — while confirming the values that are correct rather than manufacturing errors.
assertions: The audit is in French and entity names (armor type, species trait) match their French catalog labels — English names or 2014 French spellings signal a memory-sourced answer
The species ability-score bonus is identified as a 2014 rule that does not apply to a 2024 character
The stated AC of 18 is confirmed CORRECT, quoting chain mail 16 + Dex capped at 0 + shield 2; no AC error is manufactured

The stated HP of 15 is reported against the computed 14, and the provenance shows the 1/niveau x1 bonus term alongside the hit die and Con modifier — an audit that reports 13 has dropped the species bonus from the computation and fails

Arcana is flagged as absent from the fighter skill list, citing the legal set from data/classes.json (fighter-competences: acrobatics, athletics, animal-handling, history, insight, intimidation, perception, persuasion, survival) — not merely as ungranted by the background
Darkvision is flagged: the sheet states 18 m, data/species.json grants the Dwarf 36 m

The audit does not rest on the engine's lint verdict alone: a character model carries no record of what the sheet claimed, so `check` recomputes instead of comparing. Each finding is a diff the agent drew between the sheet's text and a catalog value it cites
The report states each value twice — as written on the sheet and as computed — rather than only naming the error
The output is a numbered or bulleted diff list — no new ability-score table, no new equipment block, and no 'corrected sheet' section appears

evals.prompt: is my character legal? level 1 elf druid, AC 14, HP 10, con 13, wearing leather armor, dex 14
evals.expected_output: An audit performed from values dictated in prose — the agent assembles the model itself, asks in plain language only for what is genuinely missing, and reports the diff. It must never ask the user to produce JSON.
assertions: The agent assembles the elf druid's values (AC 14, HP 10, Con 13, leather armor, Dex 14) into a character model and queries the engine before stating any verdict — the agent does not ask the user to provide JSON or a character file
At most one clarifying question appears in the agent's first response — the engine is queried for what can be computed with the stated values before asking for more
Each reported value states both the sheet's value and the computed value
Each computed value carries the engine's provenance string verbatim, not a paraphrase

evals.prompt: Vérifie cette fiche : guerrier humain niveau 1, sous-classe Briseur de Serment, don Maître d'hast.
evals.expected_output: Two different verdicts, not one: Oathbreaker is absent from the catalog ("Manquant documentaire"), while Polearm Master IS in the catalog (maitre-d-hast, img:206) and is a prerequisite violation — it requires level 4+, so a level-1 character cannot have it.
assertions: Oathbreaker is reported as absent from the catalog, and no effect is invented for it
Polearm Master is found in the catalog and reported as a prerequisite violation (level 4+ required), NOT as a missing entry
The Polearm Master effect quoted matches its catalog entry rather than being described from memory
The two cases are distinguished — a missing entry and an illegal-but-modeled entry are not conflated

A finding is reported independently of whether the subclass name resolves: no class in the catalog unlocks a subclass before level 3 (data/classes.json, subclass.level), so a level-1 fighter has no subclass at all
